card.intuition: Input tokens are everything the harness sends on each model provider request: the system prompt, conversation history, and tool results — everything the model reads before it writes. They are billed at a lower rate than output tokens but make up most of an AI-coding bill, because the stateless model re-sends the entire session every turn.
card.analogy: Input tokens are like re-printing the whole project spec for every meeting: each turn you photocopy everything said before at a discount rate, and over fifty turns the photocopying dwarfs the notes you actually write.
card.time_complexity: A single request may produce a few hundred output tokens but re-send a hundred thousand input tokens of accumulated history, so inputs dominate the bill; prefix caching shrinks it, and clearing or compacting shrinks what gets re-sent.
card.space_complexity: The session's whole history occupies the input side of the context window on every request, so accumulation decides how close you are to truncation, compaction, or a handoff.
when_to_use: Explaining a high bill when the agent barely writes anything — it's the inputs re-sending history
Deciding when to clear or compact between tasks to keep input costs down
Reasoning about prefix-cache savings where repeated history is billed as cheap cache tokens
gotchas: The input for turn fifty contains the previous forty-nine turns
Without the prefix cache you re-pay the full history as input on every request

exercise.prompt: Trace how a session's re-sent input grows: given each turn's new token count, return the total input tokens carried by the requests across all turns (each request resends everything before it).
exercise.starter_code:
def cumulative_input(turn_tokens):
    total = 0
    sent = 0
    for t in turn_tokens:
        sent = ___________
        total = total + sent
    return total
hints: Each turn's request sends the already-sent history plus this turn's new tokens
Accumulate that running sent count into the grand total turn by turn
exercise.test_code:
assert cumulative_input([10, 10, 10]) == 60
assert cumulative_input([]) == 0
assert cumulative_input([5]) == 5
